summary:
# NOTES: "The Sea Mystery" by Freeman Wills Crofts (Inspector French detective novel, Gutenberg #72771)

Single novel, 20 chapters. No multiple books.

## Ch 1: Mr. Morgan Meets Tragedy
- Burry Inlet, south Wales coast, late September evening. Mr. Morgan (small, clean-shaven, baggy Norfolk suit; manager of tin-plate works at Burry Port) fishes with son Evan (14, at school ~3 yrs).
- Only two mackerel caught. Line snags something ~20 ft deep off Llanelly, Gower (Llanrhidian Sands) side, near channel edge. Bearings taken: signal post on railway in line with west gable of large white house on hill; tall mill chimney in line with pier-head beacon.
- They grapple up a wooden crate (packing case ~3ft x 2ft x 2ft), tow it to Burry Port lifeboat slip, hammer it open at night. Smell; Morgan sees body (man in underclothes, decomposed, face battered). Morgan hides it from Evan.
- Morgan goes to police station; Sergeant Nield, Constable Williames, Smith, Watson. Coastguard Tom Manners (elderly, ex-Navy, Shoreditch origin).
- Superintendent Griffiths (Llanelly); Major Lloyd, chief constable (Llandilo). Doctors Crowth (police surgeon) and Wilbraham (friend of Lloyd's). Body 5–6 weeks dead; face obliterated; crate had steel bar ~14 in., 3–4 stone weight.
- Lloyd calls in Scotland Yard. Inspector Joseph French travels by 1.55 PM Paddington express.

## Ch 2: Inspector French Gets Busy
- French: short, stout, keen blue eyes, twinkle; believes "lead rather than drive"; friendly to Nield.
- Inquest next day at 11 am, adjourned 3 weeks.
- Body: birthmark small triangular on back of left arm near shoulder; French sketches it. Socks: left toe darned with wrong-shade wool (grey pair). Underclothes plain.
- Crate: spruce 1 inch thick, tongued and grooved, iron corner clamps; 14 nail/peg holes (7 at each of two diagonally opposite corners); label tacks form parallelogram of 8 tack heads.
- Dr. Crowth: cause = blow on back of head with soft instrument (sandbag?); face battered after death with heavy implement (hammer).
- Crowth's report: 5ft 10in, 13 stone, middle-aged (35–55), death 35–40 days earlier.
- French cites Inspector Burnley's old case (cask of murdered French wife from France).
- Theory: crate floated with holes letting in water, sank after ~1 hour. Calc: crate+body+bar = 406 lb (29 stone); displacement 985 lb; buoyancy 579 lb; holes each just under 1/6 inch (measured with pencil). Molesworth's Pocket Book borrowed.
- Morgan marks bearings on French's large-scale ordnance map.

## Ch 3: Experimental Detection
- Manners (small, stout) at Burry Port pier. Knots explained; ~5 knots ebb current; sea mile 6,080 ft (~5¾ English miles/hr).
- Loughor bridges (road: ferro-concrete, new; railway: older, timber piles), ~5 miles up estuary.
- Tide tables: August 21 (Sun) 12:05 AM high, Aug 22 (Mon) 1:23 AM, Aug 23 (Tue) 2:55 AM; neap tides (~18 ft).
- Experiment: next day (Thursday) 9:30 AM from Loughor road bridge, crate loaded with shingle equal to body weight, drifted 1 hr 7 min, passing within 50 yds of original site.
- Chief Constable Lloyd, Superintendent Griffiths attend. Boat with Manners.
- Theory: crane-lorry dropped crate from Loughor bridge on night of 21/22/23 Aug.
- Circular: lorry seen. Constable David Jenkins (Neath) saw lorry Mon 22 Aug ~8 PM, lane 2 miles north of Neath, crane-lorry with tarpaulin object; driver reddish hair, high colour, glasses, slightly over middle height, stout, workingman; said going Swansea to Merthyr Tydfil; lane leads toward Pontardawe.

## Ch 4: A Change of Venue
- Superintendent Howells (Swansea). French visits Mumbles (Head, Rams Tor, Langland Bay).
- Lorry seen: Morriston ~5 PM Mon 22 Aug (from Swansea, turned east to Neath); next morning ~10 AM patrol on Pontardulais road; 12:30 AM Mon night at Gorseinon lane (~5 miles NE of Loughor).
- Lorry owner: Llewellyn, Stepney Motor Car Co., Fisher Street, Swansea (Ford ton truck with crane). Hired ~4 PM Mon 22 Aug; letter from "Stewart", St. Pancras Hotel, London, typewritten (black ribbon); £300 deposit, £5 hire; driver returned next day 10:30, refunded £295. Driver: middling tall, stout, red hair, fresh complexion, glasses, untidy, wanted shave.
- Goods Station Morriston Road, Swansea: Sergeant Jefferies found porter; clerk Evans. Crate invoiced to "Mr. James S. Stephenson", to be called for. Sender: The Veda Office Equipment Manufacturing Co. Ltd., Ashburton, South Devon. Invoiced 16 Aug; arrived Swansea Sat 20 Aug.
- Ashburton police (Sergeant Daw): duplicator (Veda No. 3?) ordered from Euston Hotel by Stephenson, £62.10.0.
- Lorry seen again Gorseinon 9:30 PM by labourer (so didn't move).
- French leaves for Ashburton.

## Ch 5: Messrs. Berlyn and Pyke
- French at Ashburton (Silver Tiger hotel). Sergeant Daw. Veda Works at end of North Street, sales manager Mr. Fogden.
- Berlyn (Charles, junior partner, ~40, reddish hair, blue eyes, high colour) and Pyke (Stanley, travelling engineer, ~35, sallow, brown eyes/hair) vanished night Mon 15 Aug, driving to Tavistock council meeting (filing cabinets) with mill owner visit; left mill 10:50 PM. Car found ~8 miles out on moor, magneto short-circuit; footprints across moor toward Colonel Domlio's house (3/4 mile). Car found 3:35 AM by Daw.
- Mrs. Berlyn (Phyllis) woke ~3 AM.
- French: four test points: breakdown; time-table; watchman; disposal of duplicator.
- Torquay newspaper research: Western Morning News.

## Ch 6: The Despatch of the Crate
- Letter dated 12 August, Euston Hotel letterhead, typed black, signed James S. Stephenson (disguised hand); money order £62.10.0; crate to Morriston Road GWR goods station, Swansea, "to be kept till called for".
- Process: order slip with initials (storekeeper, packer, carter, goods clerk).
- Packer John Puddicoombe: crate nailed, lay overnight in packing-shed, sent next day (Tuesday 16th).
- Carter: loaded Tuesday morning, goods train 11:35 AM Plymouth route.
- Night watchman Gurney (wizened, goatee, bright eyes): on duty 7 PM–6 AM; boiler-house; rounds; says no one entered. Stokers Peter Small etc.
- Station records: crate on 11:35 train.
- French suspicious of Gurney.

## Ch 7: Dartmoor
- Sergeant Daw: Berlyn/Pyke disappearance; Makepeace garage (owner John Makepeace; son). Berlyn's car (Mercury 15-20 blue four-seater), Ardlo magneto, armature burnt out (short circuit); Makepeace claims breakdown genuine; sent to Ardlo factory, Bermondsey.
- Test drive Ashburton→Dartmeet→Two Bridges→Princetown→Dartmoor; 63 minutes.
- Test: radiator cooling ~3.5 hrs (Daw: 3–4 hrs).
- French's time-table (Tavistock 10.50 PM → Veda works ~12:05 AM → car back to moor ~2 AM). Car cold at 3:35 → impossible per French.
- Mires: Fox Tor Mire; Daw says a body would not sink if spread flat... (Ch 8).
- Colonel Domlio (45, short, thickset, dark; entomologist writing book on moor insects; Torview house).

## Ch 8: A Fresh Start
- French's new thoughts; interview Daw re Berlyn's social life. Mrs. Berlyn (Phyllis) once flirted with Pyke, then Colonel Domlio; Pyke's cousin Jefferson visited.
- Lizzie Johnston (maid; Alf Beer her beau later).
- Daw on mires: flat-lying body would float; plank idea rejected.
- Lizzie: Mrs. Berlyn couldn't sew; Lizzie mended socks. French tests her on grey sock.

## Ch 9: A Step Forward
- Mrs. Billing (Pyke's landlady, East Street) identifies underclothes & cufflinks (Pyke's), darned sock.
- London: Jefferson Pyke (17b/Kepple Street, off Russell Square) identifies birthmark (triangle sketch). Stanley Pyke confirmed as dead man. Berlyn suspected.
- Mrs. Berlyn at 70b Park Walk, Chelsea. Lincoln origins; Phyllis Considine.

## Ch 10: London's Further Contribution
- Mrs. Berlyn (Phyllis) interview; says Berlyn incapable of murder.
- Ardlo Magneto Co., Queen Elizabeth Street; Mr. Illingworth. Method: magneto armature short by needle; takes time.
- Inspector Tanner (Yard).
- Idea: spare magneto swap; Mr. Henry Armstrong (Westcliff Hotel, Bristol) ordered spare magneto, sent to St. David's Station, Exeter. Typed on same machine as duplicator letter.
- Exeter parcels office: nothing.

## Ch 11: John Gurney, Night Watchman
- Gurney's cottage at roses. Confesses slept night of 15 Aug.
- Ring at office door ~10 PM; no one visible.
- Gurney's tea doped (French experiment: gate key; can of tea).
- Gurney had key kept; only office key.

## Ch 12: The Duplicator
- Night: French at works; cards for leg castings (duplicators) altered (loop added to 6 → 8).
- Replaces faked cards with forgeries.
- Letter from Lizzie: Alf Beer (sacked packer, Berlyn dismissed him).
- Beer's story: six months ago overheard Mrs. Berlyn & Pyke in shrubbery: "I tell you 'e knows" etc.
- Office: Fogden's party alibis (Dr. Lancaster, Mrs. Lancaster, Cowls, Leacock, Miss Pym, Miss Nesbitt).
- French's theory of Berlyn's guilt; six points.

## Ch 13: The Accomplice?
- Domlio theory: Domlio as principal, Berlyn accomplice.
- Domlio interview at Torview: claims in study all evening.
- Butler John Burt, wife Sarah Burt; chauffeur Coombe; gardener Mee; lodge.
- Mrs. Burt saw Domlio come home ~2 AM, wet coat/hat.
- Coombe: car out, mud, petrol ~2 gallons.

## Ch 14: French Turns Fisherman
- Domlio admits outing: "lost miniature" of late wife, butterfly chase near Chagford; denies earlier (ashamed).
- Domlio's well: French & Daw fish with hooks; retrieve Pyke's coat (tailor tab R. Shrubsole & Co., Newton Abbot; brown tweed with purple line).
- Tailor candidates: Albert Cunningham, John Booth, Stanley Pyke, George Hepworth.

## Ch 15: Blackmail
- Pump from quarry (Mr. Glenn). Domlio present at well-pumping (42 ft deep, 12 ft water).
- Recovered: Pyke's waistcoat, trousers, shoes; duplicator parts laid on wall.
- Domlio confesses: Mrs. Berlyn's ankle twist; blackmail letter "X.Y.Z." offering photo for £50; Upper Merton glen; rendezvous Dobson's Spinney.
- Domlio lies earlier, not believed fully; French releases him with watch.

## Ch 16: Certainty at Last
- Dr. Lancaster & Mrs. Lancaster alibis: Mrs. Berlyn out ~20 min ~10 PM, through side door.
- Bicycle: Swift, Mrs. Berlyn's; Swann (gardener) saw it; pawned Plymouth 16 Aug.
- Superintendent Plymouth.
- French thinks Pyke+Phyllis accomplices; Jefferson Pyke as suspect.

## Ch 17: "Danger!"
- Ganope's tobacconist (27 Oakley Street); message "Danger. Meet me to-night at old time and place."
- Jefferson Pyke at Kepple Street; Vera Welsh (typist) typed on Corona typewriter.
- Mrs. Berlyn visits; Pyke "Jeff".

## Ch 18: On Hampstead Heath
- Hampstead Heath rendezvous. Pyke & Phyllis conversation: confession plan; Charles alive ("Poor old Charles"); escape.
- Pyke escapes via roof; Mrs. Berlyn escapes (locked room, 30 ft).

## Ch 19: The Bitterness of Death
- Typewriter copy of notes; Bibby Line "Flintshire" (Birkenhead→Marseilles); purser Hawkins (Ramsgate).
- Houston Hotel: 21 July; Stanley Pyke broke basin.
- Taxi driver William Service: fare to Victory Place (Elephant & Castle) flat 19; Mr. & Mrs. Perrin.
- French arrested? Confronted by Stanley Pyke (wearing spectacles); Pyke threatens with automatic. French tricks; struggle; Mrs. Berlyn strangles French; Carter rescues.

## Ch 20: Conclusion
- French nearly killed; Carter and Harvey.
- Pyke impersonated Jefferson; Jefferson died at Nice (appendicitis).
- Plot summary: Berlyn murdered Sun. 15 Aug (sandbagged on road); Pyke & Phyllis; Domlio framed; crate for Berlyn corpse; Pyke impersonates Jefferson.
- Pyke and Phyllis executed after assizes.
- Transcriber's note: Harper & Brothers 1928 first edition.
